analysis.title: GS Novak - U.S. Industrials & Materials Weekend Edition (11.16.26-11.20.26)
key_insights: Industrials fell almost 700bps on the week and materials were very similar. Housing-related names outperformed on sharply lower rates, while data center/AI and metals-related equities kept falling.

Notable movers: ACM +12% on strong earnings and 2027 guidance, VVV and VIK +5-6% on earnings. SMID levered industrials were hit on balance sheet and earnings concerns: TROX -42%, YSS -35%, FLY -30%, FMC -22%.
Data center names were weak: MTZ -20% after a surprise deal Friday that raises near-term leverage, and VRT, FPS and INIO each down about 18%.

2027 operating framework: lower inflation expectations, rates that have likely peaked, peak Fed hawkish commentary now and peak Fed action in December. Dollar could stay elevated, more a 2H 2027 consideration. Geopolitical tensions seen moderating.

Author expects PMIs to move higher in coming months, counter to consensus, and does not see data centers as the driver of the 10 months above 50 this year. Short cycle tends to outperform most when PMIs are between 55 and 60.

Preferred 2027 themes: aerospace as perhaps the only secular growth in industrials, defense with rising unit demand, housing exposure as a long-side hedge, and cybersecurity with limited movement despite recent events.

Avoid list: transports (supply tightness could reverse), 2026 inflation winners that become disinflation losers, agriculture with rolled-over trends and elevated valuations, and AI/data center stocks where orders and backlog KPIs are expected to weaken in 1H 2027.
November 2026 is setting up as the worst monthly performance since 2008.

Prime book: HFs net sold US equities for a third straight week, driven by heavy single-stock shorting. US single stocks saw the largest weekly shorting since Jun 2022, third largest in the past decade. 9 of 11 sectors were net sold, except Info Tech and Energy.
ETF short flows rose 11.1% this week, the largest % shorting since March and third largest in five years, led by Large Cap, Financials, Small Cap and Credit ETFs.

Mutual funds are the most overweight industrials but trimmed in Q3 and are believed to remain net sellers. Hedge funds remain overweight industrials, with length believed to sit across AI/data center.

DE reports fiscal Q4 and guides 2027 on Wed 11/25. The stock has been 50/50 on guide days. Investors expect a net income guide near $5.7bn vs standing consensus of $6.1bn. The author leans negative on DE over six months.

DE early order program was up 5% at last report, CNH and AGCO raised the bar at 15-20%, though this covers a small share of sales. North American large ag shows green shoots, Europe and Brazil remain downside risks, and crop prices have rolled over.

Week ahead: PCE, DE earnings, off-cycle earnings from AMTM, J, SYM and DY. Tech earnings from DELL, WDAY, HPQ and consumer prints from BBY, DKS, BURL, DLTR, ANF, URBN. US markets closed Thursday and close at 1pm Friday.
